items.title: UK Parliament Week, 23 to 29 November 2026
items.body: Parliament's annual week of democracy activity, with free kits for schools, youth groups and adults. Amplify plans to launch on its first day.

items.title: Votes at 16 Bill reaches Lords committee stage
items.body: The House of Lords began its Committee of the Whole House on the Representation of the People Bill on 2 November 2026, with a second day on 4 November and six days provisionally allocated. Peers can now propose changes line by line. It is not yet law.
items.source: Hansard Society, Parliament Matters Bulletin; confirm each stage on Parliament's bill page

items.title: MPs debate the review of young people and work
items.body: A review of young people and work commissioned by the Work and Pensions Secretary (the Milburn review) published its interim report in May 2026: nearly one million 16 to 24 year olds in the UK are NEET, 957,000 at the end of 2025. MPs debated it in Westminster Hall on 3 November 2026. The final report is due later in 2026.
items.source: Young People and Work interim report (GOV.UK); Hansard

items.title: April 2027 minimum wage rates announced
items.body: The Government accepted the Low Pay Commission's advice in full: £13.21 for 21 and over and £11.27 for 18 to 20, from 1 April 2027. Until then the April 2026 rates apply.

items.title: HOPELINE247 has closed
items.body: PAPYRUS Prevention of Young Suicide entered administration on 7 September 2026 and its HOPELINE247 helpline is no longer operating. The administrators point people to Samaritans (116 123), Shout (text SHOUT to 85258), NHS 111, or 999 in an emergency. This portal has removed HOPELINE247 from its helplines.

items.title: Votes at 16 Bill clears the Commons
items.body: The Representation of the People Bill completed its Commons third reading on 2 September 2026 and moved to the House of Lords. It is not yet law.
items.source: Reported by MPs and bill trackers; confirm each stage on Parliament's bill page

items.title: Social media ban for under 16s announced
items.body: The Government announced that major social media platforms will be barred from serving under 16s, with livestreaming banned for under 16s and stranger contact blocked by default for under 17s. Regulations are due before Christmas 2026, to apply from spring 2027. Campaigners under 16 should plan to work through MYPs, school councils and adult allies rather than personal accounts.
items.source: UK Government announcement, widely reported (Reuters, BBC)

items.title: 981,000 young people not earning or learning
items.body: Official estimates show around 981,000 16 to 24 year olds were NEET in April to June 2026, down from 1,012,000 in January to March, the highest since 2013.
items.source: Office for National Statistics, via Youth Futures Foundation

items.title: New minimum wage rates in force
items.body: £12.71 for 21 and over, £10.85 for 18 to 20, and £8 for under 18s and apprentices, from 1 April 2026. The 18 to 20 rate rose 8.5%.

items.title: Youth Select Committee reports on PSHE
items.body: The Youth Select Committee called on the UK Government to end the postcode lottery in PSHE teaching.

items.title: Representation of the People Bill introduced
items.body: The Government introduced the Bill that would extend the vote to 16 and 17 year olds in all UK elections.

items.title: National Youth Strategy published
items.body: Youth Matters, a ten-year strategy for 10 to 21 year olds in England (up to 25 with SEND), backed by over £500 million and shaped by over 14,000 young people.
items.source: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

items.title: UK Youth Parliament sits in the Commons
items.body: Members of Youth Parliament debated the 2025 manifesto priorities in the House of Commons Chamber in November 2025, chaired by the Speaker.
items.source: Scottish Youth Parliament and local councils' reports

items.title: National Citizen Service closed
items.body: NCS programme delivery ended on 31 March 2025 and the NCS Trust closed on 11 July 2025.

items.title: Sign Language Act (Northern Ireland) becomes law
items.body: Northern Ireland's Sign Language Act received Royal Assent on 9 July 2026, recognising both British Sign Language and Irish Sign Language and placing duties on public bodies to make information and services accessible.
